overview: Several storm systems move through the West this week, with the Pacific Northwest and Cascades getting the most snow and rain through Thursday and Friday. The Northern Rockies and Colorado see snow Friday into Saturday. The Northeast and Canada get a mix of rain and snow late in the week.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: Crystal Mountain is forecast for about 39". Mt. Bachelor and Stevens Pass follow. The National Weather Service has rain mixed in at Crystal Mountain Thursday night.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: Dry, mild weather holds through Thanksgiving. A system arrives Friday, with snow in western Wyoming through Saturday, and the snow band could shift depending on where the front stalls. Grand Targhee leads the region at 43" for the week, with its biggest day Friday at 22". Fog is likely in Jackson Hole and the Bighorn Basin Wednesday morning.

regions.title: Northeast
regions.text: Stowe is forecast for about 20", 12" of it Friday. Jay Peak and Whiteface follow. The National Weather Service has rain mixed in at Stowe Friday night.

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: Whistler is forecast for about 29". Cypress Mountain follows.

regions.title: Kootenays
regions.text: Whitewater is forecast for about 17", 11" of it Thursday. RED Mountain and Revelstoke follow.

regions.title: Tahoe
regions.text: Sugar Bowl is forecast for about 18", all of it Sunday. Kirkwood and Northstar follow. The National Weather Service has rain mixed in at Sugar Bowl Sunday and Sunday night.

regions.title: Central Rockies
regions.text: Mild, dry weather holds through Thanksgiving, and Friday is the warmest day along the Front Range. Northwest flow brings snow to the Park Range Friday and Saturday, and totals are uncertain. Steamboat peaks Saturday at 11"; Vail gets 9" that day.

regions.title: Okanagan
regions.text: Big White is forecast for about 11", 8" of it Thursday. SilverStar and Sun Peaks follow.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 11, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Nov 22–28. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
